newsitem.title: UK: U.S.Congressman praises Protestant N.Irish truce.
newsitem.headline: U.S.Congressman praises Protestant N.Irish truce.

text.p: Irish-American politician Joe Kennedy praised pro-British Loyalist leaders for their two-year truce on Thursday and said Northern Ireland would reap a rich dividend if IRA guerrilla foes restored theirs.

"I think it is important that those of us that have spoken out for the nationalist cause in the past recognise the courage that people on the Loyalist side have been showing in terms of maintaining this ceasefire," the Massachusetts congressman said starting a two-day visit to the British province.

Kennedy was speaking after talks with leaders of the Progressive Unionist Party, political wing of the outlawed Ulster Volunteer Force, and ahead of a meeting with Gerry Adams, head of the Irish Republican Army's Sinn Fein political wing.
The IRA, fighting to end British rule, ditched a 17 month ceasefire last February with bombs in Britain.

Kennedy had talks with British Northern Ireland minister Michael Ancram and walked from the Falls Road, a Catholic stronghold, to the nearby Shankill Road where he paused at a memorial for nine Protestants killed by an IRA bomb in November 1993.

The congressman, a nephew of the late President John F Kennedy, said he wanted to meet Adams "to understand what his concerns are" and discuss his views on opportunities for an IRA ceasefire and a seat for Sinn Fein in talks.
"I just want to hear directly from him what he feels is necessary to be able to achieve that," Kennedy said.

British Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday he would not permit the IRA to bomb its way into talks. Britain and Ireland say the guerrillas must call a genuine ceasefire before Sinn Fein is given a place in talks on the province's future.
U.S. President Bill Clinton has also called on the guerrillas to forsake violence.
Kennedy, stressing the affection and concern for both parts of Ireland felt by people of Irish heritage in the United States, said economic benefits would flow from peace.
"I think if we can find a ceasefire here that leads to a real peace that you are going to see enormous rewards. You are going to see companies that want to come and invest and put people to work."
PUP leader Billy Hutchinson speaking to reporters after his talks with Kennedy urged an restoration of the IRA truce, saying Loyalist patience was wearing thin.
Loyalists say an IRA bomb attack on Britain's military headquarters south of Belfast in October put pressure on their ceasefire.

John Hume, leader of the moderate Catholic Social Democratic and Labour Party, had historic first time talks with jailed Protestant guerrillas later on Thursday to bring them up to date with efforts he has made to win an IRA ceasefire.
Major recently rejected a formula put forward by Hume and Adams. An SDLP source said Hume would be "clarifying what his efforts are about".

Hutchinson told reporters: "We are in very dangerous times. I think everybody knows that the IRA have been cranking it up for some time now," Hutchinson said on the Shankill Road, the heartland of pro-British support in the province's capital.
"Everybody's expecting either a spectacular (bomb) before Christmas or something in the New Year.
"All we can do is wait and see but the Loyalist patience is running out...It is about time the IRA called their ceasefire and proved to everybody that they want peace."
